_comment: The runtime this integration is measured against. Section 18: never benchmark a release claim against a moving main. Changing any value here invalidates every real-result.json produced before the change.
commit_subject: perf(muse): let the NVFP4 prefill GEMMs run above 128 tokens (#1010)
patch_shape: insertions only; no SparkInfer line is modified or removed
_percentile_itl_note: The cb bench's percentile ITL is an INSTRUMENT addition, not a hook: it collects the per-token gaps the bench already timed into a request-local vector and prints p50/p95/p99 beside the mean and max it already printed. Request-local so the hot path takes no lock -- a mutex per decoded token across N threads would perturb the very latency being measured. The existing mean_itl_ms and max_itl_ms are untouched, so every command in results/ still means what it meant. TTF-1 scores p99_itl_ms as its tail objective, and a tail cannot be stood in for by a mean: a policy that halves the median while doubling the 99th makes serving worse and the mean better.

model.label: Qwen3.8-27B, uniform NVFP4, 17.9 GB
model._weight_bytes_per_step_note: Bytes of WEIGHTS a decode step reads, once per step however many sequences are in flight. The checkpoint's own size, in the same GB=1e9 units the bandwidth figure uses. It is here so a ceiling can say whether the step it was computed from was actually bandwidth-bound: at batch 1, 17.9 GB of weights plus 0.31 GB of state against the 18.5 GB peak bandwidth would allow in the measured 10.34 ms is 98% utilisation, so the batch-1 ceiling is tight. At sixteen sequences the same weights against a 50.6 GB implied step is 40%, and the ceiling there is a loose upper bound -- part of the step is latency and occupancy rather than bytes, and freeing recurrent traffic returns less than its arithmetic share.

The same commit and the same hook also run Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a sparse-MoE hybrid whose geometry lives in configs/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-moe-ceiling.json - the adapter derives every stride from the runtime's config, so a second model needs a geometry file and no code change.
